headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, bear the direct costs of their required grid infrastructure, preventing these expenses from being passed on to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger, environmental groups, Piedmont Environmental Council.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia Requires Data Centers to Pay for Their Own Power Lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for their required transmission infrastructure projects, preventing these billions of dollars in expenses from falling on residential ratepayers. This decision aligns with Governor Abigail Spanberger's call to shift the financial burden to large energy users.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandated
short_summary: This legislation requires water users supplying data centers to report their total water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for transparency and environmental monitoring.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local communities.
opponents: Data center industry, Taxpayers Protection Alliance.
news_headline: Virginia Mandates Data Center Water Use Reporting
news_summary: Senate Bill 553 requires water users providing water to data centers to report total potable and reclaimed water volumes to the State Water Control Board. This aims to provide data on data center water consumption, which some critics argue is depleting regional resources.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residences and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents concerned about noise and environmental impact.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: New Virginia Laws Address Data Center Noise and Siting
news_summary: HB 153, passed in Virginia, creates a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring sound profile assessments near homes and schools. This legislation responds to growing community concerns about noise pollution and allows localities to assess broader environmental impacts before approving data center projects.
